Because expense growth outpaced revenue, GAAP operating income, pretax income, consolidated net income and net income attributable to Equifax all fell in sequence. The segment mix is genuinely mixed: Workforce Solutions revenue declined on lower Verification Services, while U.S. Information Solutions and International revenue both increased, so the flat consolidated top line masks offsetting segment moves. The supported research implication is that the near-term earnings trajectory is more sensitive to the expense line than to revenue, and that the Workforce Solutions softness is a specific area to test against the next disclosure rather than a consolidated revenue problem.","counterevidence":"The opposing evidence is real and should not be minimized: consolidated revenue did not decline, and two of the three reported segments grew sequentially, with International and U.S. Information Solutions both contributing positively. Employer Services revenue edged up, so the Workforce Solutions decline is attributable to Verification Services rather than to the whole workforce franchise. No source-explicit driver links the expense increase to any cause, so causal attribution remains unresolved rather than established. Evidence that would change the view: the full Form 10-Q including segment operating income and margin detail, the MD&A discussion of the selling, general and administrative increase, non-GAAP reconciliations, year-over-year comparatives, and any disclosed restructuring, litigation, technology or acquisition costs; if those show the expense step-up is discrete and non-recurring while Verification Services softness is transient, the negative read would weaken materially, whereas confirmation of a structural cost or pricing issue in Verification Services would strengthen it."},"asserted_state":{"review_id":"tr_cb887485827f4df385da","evidence_ids":["RS-EFX-Q2","RS-EFX-Q3"],"next_review_at":null,"decision_hold":true,"actionability":"blocked","alert_status":"acknowledged"}}

reviews.rationale: Sequential comparison of selected GAAP consolidated rows shows revenue essentially flat while total operating expenses rose, concentrated in selling, general and administrative expense, with smaller increases in depreciation and amortization and a slight decline in cost of services. The expense growth outpaced revenue, so GAAP operating income, pretax income, consolidated net income and net income attributable to Equifax all declined sequentially. The tax provision line moved in the direction of a larger provision, which is not a smaller tax drag and does not offset the pretax decline. Segment rows show a mixed picture: Workforce Solutions revenue declined on lower Verification Services, while U.S. Information Solutions and International revenue increased, so the consolidated revenue total was roughly unchanged. No source-explicit driver links the expense increase to a specific cause; the selected rows contain no management commentary, no non-GAAP or adjusted measures, no guidance, and no year-over-year comparatives, so margin and cost explanations remain unresolved attribution.
